references.text: In Matthew's parallel account of the Sadducees' question about the resurrection, it is likewise said that eventually the woman also died ([ref:Matt 22:27|Matthew 22:27]). The same sequence of events in this synoptic parallel.

Mark's parallel tells the same story: none of the seven brothers left any children, and eventually the woman also died ([ref:Mark 12:22|Mark 12:22]). This is the second synoptic parallel to Luke 20:32.

The background for the entire story is the law of levirate marriage in [ref:5 Mos 25:5-10|Deuteronomy 25:5-10], which required a brother to marry his deceased brother's widow if he died childless. The woman's death after all seven brothers concludes the hypothetical scenario constructed by the Sadducees based on this law.

The book of Ruth provides an example of the levirate principle in practice. Naomi lost her husband and her two sons, leaving her daughters-in-law as widows without children ([ref:Rut 1:3-5|Ruth 1:3-5]). The situation in the Sadducees' question is reminiscent of this.

The story of Tamar in [ref:1 Mos 38:6-11|Genesis 38:6-11] is an early example of levirate practice where several brothers died one after another, and the woman outlived them. This forms a narrative background for the hypothetical scenario in Luke 20.
